proofs.argument: The invariance pair (grant Hold vs grant Accept) has DIFFERENT images under the uniform A-IDX translations EJ-A-BER-2 and EJ-A-WL-2, which preserve outcomes on all of MC-EJ. The original argument quantified only over translations with one adjudication task per output.

proofs.statement: Original EJ-7: disposition-specific authorization NOT-EXPRESSIBLE in Regime A for Bertino and W&L.

proofs.argument: (i) m1/m2 differ in a 1-local feature (allowed edge from start into a goal), so an element-local translation can separate them; identical images were shown only for translations ignoring edge endpoints. (ii) Exact WSP reductions exist (NAP-R-WSP-LABEL, NAP-R-WSP-PATH); they repurpose users, so they violate R3, but they show the obstacle is the sort discipline, not expressive power.
proofs.statement: Original NAP-3: NAP not expressible in WSP/R2BAC under R3, by an invariance pair.
proofs.status: REFUTED as stated; NON-EXPRESSIBILITY NOT ESTABLISHED for WSP

proofs.argument: Machine check: graphs A and B have identical multisets of r-types (r = 1, 2) but NAP(A) != NAP(B).
proofs.assumptions: T_loc(r): includes WSP translations in which every step has a single authorised user and every constraint is generated from an r-neighbourhood (verdict = conjunction of locally fixed truth values). Does NOT cover translations with >= 2 candidate users per step (CSP search is global) -- see NAP-R-WSP-LABEL.
proofs.statement: No translation whose target verdict is a function of the multiset of radius-r neighbourhood types of the DEA state graph (labels: start, goal, authorised) preserves NAP, for r = 1, 2 (and any r with L, M > 2r+1).
proofs.status: PROVEN-NON-EXPRESSIBLE under stated assumptions (class T_loc(r), r<=2 checked)

proofs.argument: The permit/deny verdict for an event in instance W is a function of W's CB, spec and history, all of which are functions of W's own event projection. The witness gives two models with identical projection of W up to the event and different DEA verdicts; hence any A-INST-LOCAL translation errs on one of them. Dropping A-INST-LOCAL (LED-A-BER-MERGE, LED-B-BER) removes the obstruction.
proofs.assumptions: A-INST-LOCAL; Def 4.7 (CB(W) per workflow); execution predicates range over the activations of W only (Tab. II: 'within a workflow').
proofs.statement: No Bertino translation preserves the ledger if each DEA workflow maps to its own Bertino instance and the constraint base and facts of an instance are functions of that instance's own events (A-INST-LOCAL).

proofs.argument: Lemma (monotonicity): adding fresh users and relation pairs that each contain a fresh user leaves UR, SA and every relation on old users unchanged, so every valid (partial) plan over old users stays valid. [VP-2] The pair m0/m1 is insufficient (a translation adding (y,z) for every z on each edge x->y is exact on m0 and m1). DEA pair: m1 (p->a in theta_E, p->j in theta_J: conflict) and m2 (p->a in theta_E, o->j in theta_J: no conflict). By GENERICITY the images agree on acting users {a,j}; by the lemma pairs on non-acting users do not affect the run, so the target errs on one. Machine check: lemma verified on all enumerated 2-step instances with one fresh user; pair verified.
proofs.assumptions: W&L-07 Defs 1-5; A-STEP; LOCAL-REL; GENERICITY (the contribution of an edge is invariant under renaming non-acting principals); both DEA closure readings.
proofs.statement: No W&L-07 translation preserves ExecConflict if (A-STEP) steps, order, SA and constraints depend only on DEA acts and grants, not on the set of non-acting principals, and (LOCAL-REL) each control edge contributes only pairs containing its endpoints.
proofs.status: PROVEN-NON-EXPRESSIBLE under stated assumptions (A-STEP + LOCAL-REL + GENERICITY) [VP-2]

proofs.argument: Boundary model: p->o only at t=2, o->j only at t=3, p->a in theta_E. A: no conflict; B: conflict. Disagreements inside MC-CTRL: 72 of 16807.
proofs.assumptions: Windows theta_E=[0,1], theta_J=[2,3]; MC-CTRL with 7 interval options.
proofs.statement: Per-instant closure (A) and window-union closure (B) give different ExecConflict decisions; DEA v0.3.4.3 p.8 does not select either.
